About CMI: Central Moloney has been a trailblazer in manufacturing distribution transformers and transformer components since 1949. Our ISO 9001-certified legacy is built on delivering top-notch products, on-time reliability, and pushing the boundaries of excellence. Join us in powering a future resonating with Central Moloney 's strength.
About the Role: The Key Account Manager develops CMI’s transformer components business in Latin America, prioritizing Mexico and South America, and pursues selected international opportunities. The role focuses on transformer OEMs and approved commercial partners, combining new customer acquisition, strategic account management, and market development with product management responsibilities for assigned component families.
Reporting to the Senior Vice President Sales, U.S., the KAM builds market intelligence, establishes customer access, leads product qualification, and converts opportunities into profitable orders. • Own assigned international bookings and gross-margin objectives. Lead opportunity qualification, bid strategy, customer presentations, pricing recommendations, negotiations, and commercial closure within delegated authority.

• Coordinate complete technical and commercial quotations with Inside Sales and the components team. Obtain required approvals for discounts, contractual exceptions, and customer-specific commitments.

• Evaluate freight, duties, currency, payment, credit, and delivery assumptions with Finance and logistics. Coordinate export requirements with the responsible specialists and ensure approved terms are reflected in the offer.

• Validate product requirements with Engineering and delivery commitments with Operations. Support order handoff and maintain customer communication on changes, quality concerns, and recovery actions.

• Maintain accurate opportunities, forecasts, account activity, and win/loss feedback in designated systems, using CRM when available. Report country and account performance and recommend actions to improve growth and margin.

• Product management duties: Gather customer requirements, recommend product improvements, develop business cases, coordinate the product roadmap and launches,

title: Area Director SE
description:

Work Authorization: Must be authorized to work in the U.S.A. for any employer. Travel: Up to 50% of time within the U.S. Frequent domestic and some international travel required. Frequent weekend and evening work to accommodate donor schedules. May require trips to hazardous locations. Estimated Salary Range: $87,700 to $124,560
THE JOB
The Area Director will maximize World Vision’s ministry by developing long-term, effective relationships with individuals and family foundations giving $25,000 or more per year in financial resources, with the goal of providing them with a deeper understanding of holistic needs in the world and boldly challenging them to respond sacrificially to those needs through the ministry of World Vision. Help carry out our Christian organization’s mission, vision, and strategies. Personify the ministry of World Vision by witnessing to Christ and ministering to others through life, deed, word and sign.

• Work with gift planning staff to set up donor-advised funds, stock gifts, wills, etc.

• Represent WVUS in various settings, including speaking engagements directly related to major gift development and media interviews to spread the word about WV’s domestic and international ministry.

• Attend and participate in job related training programs as assigned.

• Work collaboratively with team members when assigned to work as a member of a team.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

• Maintain awareness of corporate goals, objectives, organizational announcements, and activities. Reference and follow organizational policies and procedures, seeking clarity as needed.

YOU BRING THESE SKILLS

• Networking: Builds and sustains an active network of contacts Readily engages others and builds rapport, trust and positive relationships by understanding others’ business and personal needs.

• Prospecting Skills: Effectively asks questions and listens to donors to identify giving opportunities. Changes approach to produce the desired result. Qualifies donors as to their giving potential. Proactively contacts others, despite risk of rejection.

The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.

We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

• Writes, reviews, and provides feedback/direction to others involved in the content development process (eg, Medical Writers, Editors, Graphic Artists) to ensure that the content meets the objectives and strategic needs of the Strategic Account Director and client and adheres to the established Precision AQ standards

• Analyzes, interprets, and utilizes complex medical documents; reviews analyses conducted by junior team members

title: Director of Product Experience & Design - India
description:
All roles at JumpCloud® are Remote unless otherwise specified in the Job Description.
About JumpCloud®
JumpCloud® is the AI-powered unified IT management platform designed to secure the modern workforce. By consolidating identity, device, and access management, JumpCloud provides intelligent, secure IT that scales from human users to autonomous AI agents. We help organizations around the globe eliminate complexity and turn AI risk into an optimized advantage, ensuring the right people and agents have secure access to the right resources at all times.
 
JumpCloud is Intelligent, Secure IT.

The role
Every organization now runs on identities, devices and, increasingly, AI agents. Someone has to decide who and what gets access to what, and keep it secure. At JumpCloud, that is often a small IT team responsible for an entire workforce across Mac, Windows, Linux and mobile, using one platform in place of several. For them, the experience is the product. When it is clear, a lean team runs what once took a stack of tools and a much larger staff. When it is not, people get locked out and risks go unseen.
That experience will change more in the next two years than in the last ten. Admins will ask an assistant instead of opening a console. AI agents will need identities, permissions and oversight of their own. Some of our most important experiences will have no screen at all.
We are looking for the design leader who will define what comes next. You will set the experience vision for the platform, decide where design invests across the interface, AI and headless experiences, and build a team known for its craft and its judgment. You will sit with Product and Engineering leadership as an equal partner, and your measure will be simple: how much easier, safer and faster our customers' work becomes.

#LI-PS1

JumpCloud is committed to being Remote First, meaning that you are able to work remotely within the country noted in the Job Description.
 
This role is remote in the country of India. You must be located in and authorized to work in India to be considered for this role.

JumpCloud® has teams in 15+ countries around the world and conducts our internal business in English. The interview and any additional screening process will take place primarily in English. To be considered for a role at JumpCloud®, you will be required to speak and write in English fluently.  Any additional language requirements will be included in the details of the job description.
 
Why JumpCloud?  
If you thrive working in a fast, SaaS-based environment and you are passionate about solving challenging technical problems, we look forward to hearing from you! JumpCloud® is an incredible place to share and grow your expertise! You’ll work with amazing talent across each department who are passionate about our mission. We’re out of the box thinkers, so your unique ideas and approaches for conceiving a product and/or feature will be welcome. You’ll have a voice in the organization as you work with a seasoned executive team, a supportive board and in a proven market that our customers are excited about.  
 
One of JumpCloud®'s three core values is to “Build Connections.” To us that means creating " human connection with each other regardless of our backgrounds, orientations, geographies, religions, languages, gender, race, etc. We care deeply about the people that we work with and want to see everyone succeed." - Rajat Bhargava, CEO

JumpCloud® is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.

We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.

We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. Location: Remote, United States
Role Type: Full-Time
Reporting to: Chief Product Officer

• Base salary: $165,000 to $200,000

• Total compensation includes the base salary plus a guaranteed supplement

The Senior Director of Curriculum is a senior leadership role responsible for the vision, strategy, and execution of CodePath ’s entire curriculum portfolio. You will set long-term curriculum direction while directly shaping high-impact courses, particularly in AI-native software engineering, technical interview preparation, cybersecurity, and web development.
You will partner closely with Learning (Programs & Student Experience), Engineering, Platform, Revenue, and Employer Partnerships to ensure CodePath courses remain rigorous, engaging, and aligned to rapidly evolving industry needs. Software engineering is changing faster than traditional academic programs can adapt. Generative AI is reshaping how engineers design, build, debug, and ship software-and employers increasingly expect new graduates to be AI-native from day one.
As Director of Curriculum, you will define how CodePath bridges the gap between academic computer science programs and industry expectations. You will lead the transition to a more modular, flexible curriculum architecture that enables rapid iteration, targeted updates, and new delivery models across:

• Undergraduate, for-credit university partnerships

Company Overview:
Our client is a small, founder-led consumer brand based in Austin, TX, that makes a regulated nicotine product (tobacco-free pouches) and sells it direct-to-consumer in the UK. Because Meta, Google, and TikTok all prohibit nicotine advertising, there is no ad budget this company can spend to buy growth - every channel that's left (search, owned email and SMS, subscription retention, referral, retail and trade, athlete and podcast partnerships, field sampling) has to be built and wired together by hand. That constraint is the whole shape of this job.
Your Role:
This role exists because the easy version of growth marketing isn't available here - someone has to build the campaign machinery, not just brief it. You'll spend real time each week directing Claude Code to connect APIs, enrich lists, and automate recurring work, and the rest of your time running campaigns alongside the people actually knocking on doors: sales, field, and partnerships. You report directly to the two founders, at manager level, fully hands-on, with no reports of your own (headcount comes later, if at all). Success looks like a trade and partnership outbound engine that runs itself, a field team that's armed and getting better each cycle, owned channels (search, lifecycle, retention, referral) doing the growth work that paid acquisition can't, and numbers everyone can actually trust.
A note on the category: this is a regulated product, and the rules aren't style guidance - they're hard constraints on the job itself. No health, cessation, or performance claims anywhere, ever. Age and territory gating (18+, UK only) stays intact, full stop. No paid social or paid search for the product, no workarounds. Nothing overstated in writing. If that reads as a limitation on the work rather than the actual shape of it, this isn't the right seat.
You'll:

• Build and run the trade and partnership outbound engine - define the segment, pull and enrich the list, verify and score contacts, write and track the sequence, and know when not to use a sequencer (some outreach has to go out by hand)

• Arm the field team (sampling, shop visits, trade shows) with target lists, routes, one-pagers, and post-visit follow-up sequences, then work alongside them so the next version is better

• Own the channels that are actually open here: search and content, lifecycle email and SMS, subscription retention (win-back, dunning recovery, pause-instead-of-cancel), and referral programs, including the reconciliation behind them

• Produce creative in-house with AI tools against the brand's existing visual system - knowing when to generate, when to composite a real product shot instead, and when to send a piece to a human

• Automate anything manual and recurring - enrichment scripts, list hygiene, report pulls, campaign QA, content pipelines - instead of adding it to someone's checklist

• Own first-party measurement (order and subscription data, cohort retention, referral attribution, search visibility), since no ad platform is feeding this business conversion data, and flag a bad number before anyone else finds it

You Bring:

• Real, hands-on experience directing Claude Code (or an equivalent coding agent) on live work - connected to an API or MCP server, shipping something still in use today. This is the one non-negotiable requirement on this list, and it's tested directly in the interview process; nearly everything else here is trainable

• 3+ years hands-on in marketing - the profile that fits typically started in a coordinator-type role, got tired of waiting on others to pull data or wire up tools, and taught themselves to do it

• Cold outbound you've run yourself, start to finish: built the list, wrote the sequence, watched the reply rate, fixed deliverability when it broke, using Apollo or an equivalent plus at least one sequencer

• Comfortable with data - you read a CSV without flinching, write SQL or get there with help, and know why a bad join can quietly doub

title: Trust Communications

TL;DR

Millions of people build on Lovable, from software that runs new businesses to the tools that power existing ones. At the center of it all is trust. That’s why we’re looking for an exceptional storyteller to spearhead Lovable’s trust, safety, and security communications efforts.

WHY LOVABLE

For decades, the ability to build software belonged to a tiny fraction of the population: the people with the credentials, the technical training, the access. Everyone else had to wait, or pay, or give up. Lovable is the counterargument: We exist for the people with ideas who were locked out of software creation until now.

Over 70 million projects have been built on the platform. Hundreds of thousands of people pay for it. The product handles real infrastructure, not only prototypes: authentication, databases, payments, and deployment. People run real businesses on Lovable, which means the stakes are real too.

The comms challenge: when anyone can build, the platform has to be safe for everyone who does, and they need to know it. That takes someone who can tell the story of how we think about topics like safety, security, and reliability before anyone asks, and who can be honest, precise, and fast when the questions come up anyway.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Build and own Lovable’s trust narrative. You’ll own Lovable’s trust narrative in earned, new, and owned media, proactively telling the story of how we think about security, privacy, and safety. You’ll shape the stories that highlight our commitments and ensure we show up in the conversations where trust in AI platforms is being decided right now.

Be the comms partner to our security and trust leadership. You’ll develop and own the spokesperson platforms for our CISO and other senior leaders who speak on our trust efforts, identifying and preparing them for on-stage and media opportunities. You’ll help them become recognized voices on topics of trust in AI software creation.

Own incident communications, end to end. When something doesn’t go as planned, you’re the incident comms lead who ensures clear and swift communications for every audience that needs to hear from us, including media, customers, and employees. WHO YOU ARE

You’ve done trust, safety, or security communications. You have proven comms experience across a variety of trust-related topics, from AI safety to security. You’ve worked on or alongside security, privacy, or trust and safety teams.

You have real incident experience. You’ve been the incident comms lead more than once, and you’ve probably written a playbook along the way. You bring the attention to detail, precision, speed, and judgment an incident requires.

You have strong media relationships in the tech and AI ecosystem. Security and trust reporters, analysts, policy-adjacent media, perhaps even researchers. You know who they are, what they care about, and how to earn their attention honestly.

You’re voraciously curious. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you need to be willing to understand how a platform like ours works well enough to describe an incident accurately and explain a safety decision without hand-waving.

You write clearly and have keen attention to detail. Your writing is precise, human, and accessible, even when the subject matter is complex or the situation is sensitive. You also catch things others may miss.

You’re calm, hands-on, and low-ego. You’ll draft the statements, build the media list, prep the spokesperson, and coordinate across teams yourself. You thrive in environments where the plan often changes and the pace is relentless.

Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench.

As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper.

- Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency.

- Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail.

- Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously.

- Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems.

- Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production.

- Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field.

- A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP.

- Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show.

- Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks).

- High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running.

- Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research.

EVEN BETTER

- Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue.

- Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes.

- Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization.

- Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models.

- Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks.

title: Senior Recruiter
Research Engineer, Index Intelligence
description:
Exa is an applied AI lab building a search engine unlike the world has ever seen. We build massive-scale infra to crawl the entire web, train state-of-the-art embedding models to process it, and design super high performant vector databases to retrieve over it. We now power search for Cursor, Cognition, HubSpot, and over 400,000 developers and have raised $350m from Lightspeed, Benchmark, and a16z.

 

Our ultimate goal is to build perfect search over all the world's information, far beyond Google. If you want to build massive-scale ML systems that will define the way the new AI world consumes information, this is the place for you.

We crawl the web continuously and cannot keep all of it, refresh all of it, or spend a GPU on all of it. Something has to decide which pages are worth indexing, which links are worth following, which pages say the same thing as pages we already have, what has gone stale, and what we should never have picked up. These decisions are worth more than most ranking work. The cheapest way to improve search is to stop indexing pages nobody should ever retrieve, and to start indexing the ones we are missing. Today they run on a mix of learned signals and thresholds someone picked.

We are looking for a research engineer to own the signals behind those decisions, and the decisions themselves.

DESIRED EXPERIENCE

- You are comfortable owning a problem with no ground truth, where the first job is defining what the right answer means

- Hands-on ML experience with classifiers, rankers and calibration, plus strong data instincts at web scale

- You think in end-to-end impact. A signal only counts if a decision changes and search gets better

- You like working across teams. Crawling, indexing and retrieval all consume what you build

- You care about the problem of finding high quality knowledge and recognize how important this is for the world

EXAMPLE PROJECTS

- Make parsing work on the pages where it currently does not, and prove the improvement rather than assert it

- Teach a model to judge page quality, and get everyone to agree on what quality means well enough to supervise it

- Work on credibility and misinformation as a modelling problem: what a page claims, whether it is a reliable source of it, and whether it was written for a reader or for a crawler

- Decide whether two documents are semantically the same or genuinely different, so we can deduplicate the web without collapsing pages that a user would want to see separately

title: Brand Director
description:
We're a group of friends building apps for friends, and we think friendship deserves a better place online. Our brand is how the world first meets that idea, usually in a three-second scroll, in a language that isn't ours, on a phone in a city we've never been to.

We're looking for a Brand Lead who writes like a dream and ships like a machine. Someone who's run global campaigns at a top agency, knows what a great brief feels like, and is ready to trade the client side of the table for owning the whole thing.

You'll shape how amo sounds, looks and shows up everywhere, from a two-word push notification to a launch film watched in fifteen countries.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Own the amo voice. Write it, guard it, and make it better every week. App copy, launch posts, store listings, social, scripts, the little lines that make people smile.

- Run global campaigns end to end. From the first idea on a napkin to the last cut in market, across Europe, the US and beyond.

- Brief and push creative partners. Agencies, directors, creators and our in-house design team. You know how to get their best work because you've been on their side of the table.

- Make the brand local without making it boring. Adapt ideas so they land in Paris, London, LA and Seoul, not just translate them.

- Measure what the brand is really doing. Set up and run brand tracking across our markets, following awareness, consideration and perception over time, and turn what you learn into the next brief.

- Work in days, not weeks. Spot a moment on Tuesday, have a campaign live on Thursday, learn from it on Friday.

- Sweat the details. Easter eggs, onboarding screens, the name of a feature. Small words do big work here.

WHAT THAT MAY LOOK LIKE:

Kicking off a campaign with an agency for our next market launch, and setting up the tracker that tells us a month later whether people there know who we are and like what they see.

WHO YOU ARE:

- A writer first. You can make a headline sing and kill your darlings without blinking. Your portfolio proves it.

- Agency-trained. You've spent real time at a creative agency and worked on brands people actually know. You've sat in the pitch, survived the feedback round and shipped anyway.

- Global from day one. You've led or played a key role in campaigns that ran across several markets at once, and you know what changes (and what never should) from one country to the next.

- Fast and opinionated. Conviction over consensus. You'd rather put out something great today than something perfect next month.

- Fluent in internet. You know what's trending before it trends, and you can tell the difference between a moment worth joining and one worth skipping.

- Bilingual or better is a plus. English is our working language. French, Spanish, Portuguese, Korean or Japanese would make us very happy.

BONUS POINTS IF:

You've worked on a consumer app, built a brand from scratch, or have a group chat that's funnier than most ad campaigns.

WHY AMO:

- You'll own it. No account director, no client sign-off chain. Your ideas go from your head to millions of phones.

- You'll move fast. We make decisions quickly and learn from mistakes even quicker. Intense, but healthy.

- You'll be in good company. Over half the team is international, with 25 nationalities and counting. One in four of us moved cities or countries to be here.

- You'll grow x10. Colleagues across product, design, engineering and growth will challenge your work every day, and you'll do the same to theirs.

- You'll have backing. We're supported by some of the best tier-1 investors in the world and growing at a pace our space hasn't seen in years.

LIFE AT AMO:

To ensure that everyone is set up for success within our way of working, we work together onsite 5 days a week. We wanted to make sure coming to the office is as comfortable as possible for you:

- We chose a location in central Paris, near Opera (Metro lines 3,8,9 and RER A).

- We have a beautiful Parisian-style office

You will own the qualified pipeline number paid spend produces end to end, deciding where to lean in, where to cut, and when to ask for more budget with evidence rather than instinct.

HYBRID

We follow a hybrid work model, and for this role there is an expectation of 2-3 days per week in our NYC or SF office. Candidates should be based within a commutable distance, as we believe in the value of in person collaboration and building strong team connections while also supporting flexibility where possible.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own Middesk's paid demand engine end to end: paid search, paid social, display/retargeting, intent and review-site placements, and sponsored content

- Build a unified paid budget and channel mix, and manage the agency relationship as a vendor executing against your strategy, not as the strategy itself

- Build a CAC and payback model by channel and segment that ties spend directly to qualified pipeline and revenue, not clicks, impressions, or MQLs

- Run a test-and-kill system: a standing queue of channel, audience, and creative tests, with a cadence for reallocating budget toward what's working and cutting what isn't

- Partner with EPD to build and iterate paid-specific landing pages and conversion tracking, distinct from the organic site experience but reporting into the same funnel instrumentation

- Document the standard for which campaigns flex to support the Named Accounts motion (ads orchestrated around target accounts) and which run independently, and keep a shared calendar with that team

- Build the case for scaling spend: real numbers proving the next dollar still pays back before asking for materially more budget

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

- Senior IC role 5+ years of hands-on paid acquisition experience or demand gen marketing

- A strategic thinker who can see the whole paid motion, channel mix, measurement, creative, and landing pages, and build one coordinated system rather than optimize a single channel in isolation

- A track record of personally owning a number end to end in a high-growth environment, with real budget accountability, not just channel execution

- Has run paid media across more than one channel at real budget, not just "a Google Ads person" or "a LinkedIn ads person"

- Enough measurement discipline to defend a CAC and payback model to the CEO or CRO directly, and comfortable killing a channel that isn't working even when it's familiar

- Enough technical fluency to hold an agency account

description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Horizons

The Horizons team leads Anthropic's reinforcement learning (RL) research and development, playing a critical role in advancing our AI systems. We've contributed to every Claude release, with significant impact on the autonomy, coding, and reasoning capabilities of Anthropic's models.

 

About the role

We're hiring for the Cybersecurity RL team within Horizons. As a Research Engineer, you'll help to safely advance the capabilities of our models in secure coding, vulnerability remediation, and other areas of defensive cybersecurity.

This role blends research and engineering, requiring you to both develop novel approaches and realize them in code. Your work will include designing and implementing RL environments, conducting experiments and evaluations, delivering your work into production training runs, and collaborating with other researchers, engineers, and cybersecurity specialists across and outside Anthropic.

The role requires domain expertise in cybersecurity paired with interest or experience in training safe AI models. For example, you might be a white hat hacker who's curious about how LLMs could augment or transform your work, a security engineer interested in how AI could help harden systems at scale, or a detection and response professional wondering how models could enhance defensive workflows.

 

You may be a good fit if you:

•
Have experience in cybersecurity research.

•
Have experience with machine learning.

•
Have strong software engineering skills.

•
Can balance research exploration with engineering implementation.

•
Are passionate about AI's potential and committed to developing safe and beneficial systems.

•
Professional experience in security engineering, fuzzing, detection and response, or other applied defensive work.

Experience participating in or building CTF competitions and cyber ranges.

Academic research experience in cybersecurity.

Familiarity with RL techniques and environments.

Familiarity with LLM training methodologies.

title: Senior Salesforce Developer, Lead to Quote
description:
About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.

SUMMARY:

Delinea's global go-to-market organization runs on Salesforce, covering the full Lead-to-Quote lifecycle from first touch through territory planning, partner selling and quoting. Salesforce sits at the center of a broader GTM ecosystem of partner, forecasting, sales engagement and data tools.

You will be the senior technical owner on the Lead-to-Quote Business Systems team. Requests from Global Go-to-Market Operations, Marketing and Channel teams often arrive as a loose set of requirements. You will work with stakeholders and the Business Systems team to refine them, decide whether the answer is configuration, Flow, Apex, Lightning Web Components, an integration, or something outside Salesforce, and then get it built. Often that means writing it yourself; sometimes it means pairing with or guiding an Admin or Developer through it.

This is a hands-on role. You will also review code and designs, set patterns others build on, and make the Admins and Developers around you stronger.

TWO HALVES OF ONE JOB

We are explicit by design. Roughly 70% of your time is hands-on design, build, test and support. Roughly 30% is technical leadership: refining requirements with the Business Systems team, design and code review, and mentoring. The split shifts with the quarter.

This is not an architecture-only role, and it is not a people-management role. You will not supervise a team or assign its work. You will own hard problems and raise the bar for the people solving them with you.

THE PROBLEMS YOU'LL SOLVE

• Turn loose requirements into sound designs. Working with stakeholders, subject matter experts and our Business Systems Analysts, you get to the real problem, bring two or three options with the tradeoffs named, recommend one, and land on a design the business agrees with and the team can build.

• Decide configure, automate, code or integrate. Some problems belong in Flow. Others need Apex, LWC, an integration, or another system. You make the call, write down why, and see it through, whether you build it or guide someone else who does.

• Make integrations fail loudly and recover. Authentication, async processing, retries, error handling and monitoring, so a failure shows up as an alert and not as bad data three weeks later.

• Untangle what has grown too complicated. Overlapping automation, duplicated logic and brittle customizations, replaced with patterns the team can read and support.

• Raise the security bar on Salesforce and its integrations. We are an identity security company, and our own systems should show it. You will tighten access to least privilege, move integrations to secure authentication with scoped integration users, and make sure every external connection has an owner and a reason to exist.

• Ship changes people trust. Flow, Apex, LWC or configuration, every change moves through source control, review and testing with evidence attached.

Our customers vary in type and size, and our goal is to unlock exceptional value for everyone. title: Fund Banking Lead
description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books - all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Fund Banking Lead to build and own the motion to win emerging fund managers and their LPs as customers and partners, end to end.

Your accountability in one sentence: make Rho the leading choice for new fund managers. That means winning GPs as customers of Rho's fund banking platform - yield on called capital, cash back on operating spend, up to $75M in FDIC insurance, every entity in one login - and building the path to serve their portfolio companies, which sit squarely in Rho's core ICP.

This is a build-from-zero seat on the Partnerships team. You'll report to our Head of Partnerships and work daily across VC Partnerships, Product, and Sales, in our SF or NYC offices.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own Rho's fund banking strategy: map the comprehensive approach to win - budget, conferences, gaps, and opportunities - and keep it honest as the market moves.

- Build the network: develop and run the relationships with GPs, LPs, and allies that win GPs as customers.

- Turn GP wins into portfolio wins: create the path from a signed fund to banking its portfolio companies, in partnership with Sales.

- Be the bridge between VC Partnerships, Product, and Sales - carry learnings and opportunities in both directions so the whole company gets sharper at winning funds.

- Be Rho's visible leader in the emerging-manager and LP universe - in the right rooms, from LP gatherings to emerging-manager conferences - so new fund managers know Rho before their first capital call.

WHAT YOU BRING

- Deep proximity to GPs and LP relationships - for example as a chief of staff to a GP, in investor relations, or in capital formation - and a real understanding of emerging fund managers' pain points. Domain background is strongly preferred.

- Relationship-first with family office and LP audiences. You win trust over years; an aggressive startup-sales style is not how you operate, because it doesn't translate in these rooms.

- Credible and visible in the emerging-manager community - people in that world already take your call.

- A builder's temperament: you'd rather map the market and run the play yourself than wait for a playbook.

- You already use AI to move faster - research, drafting, pipeline hygiene - and you're curious what's next.

- Based in New York City or San Francisco and excited to work in office with the team.

- Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time.

NICE TO HAVE

- Time as an emerging manager / VC, or working at a fund administrator, bank, or fintech serving venture funds.

The budgeted total cash compensation range for this role is $180-220K, split between base and variable, plus meaningful equity compensation.

Compensation may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to cash compensation, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

Diversity is a core value at Rho. We're passionate about building and sustaining an inclusive and equitable environment for all those involved with our mission, including employees, contractors, candidates, customers and vendors. We believe every member of the Rho community enriches our ability to provide a broad range of ways to understand and engage with the market, identify problems, and drive solutions that align with our mission. title: Sr. Model Engineer
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

Sr. Model Engineer

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. We train frontier coding agents and scale RL on real user data to make them increasingly effective. We're looking for Research Scientists who can drive effective RL or mid-training research in a small-team setting. You'll own ambiguous, hard research problems end-to-end: forming hypotheses, designing experiments, building the training/eval/data needed to test them, and pushing results into the next model.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Design and run rigorous experiments that turn research ideas into measurable gains in model capability

- Improve data recipes through data quality, deduplication, and mixture experiments

- Define what makes RL data and rewards good, including grader design and preventing reward hacking

- Advance training science, from architecture and scaling experiments to post-training recipes for coding and computer-use agents

- Build evals and targeted tasks that expose model weaknesses and guide where the team invests next

- Partner with engineers to take promising results from small experiments to frontier-scale training runs

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- 3+ years of hands-on experience training or post-training large neural networks (1B+ parameters), including work on pre-training, fine-tuning, or RL-based methods (e.g., RLHF, DPO).

- Experience writing production-quality code in Python, PyTorch, JAX, Rust, or C++

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Able to handle ambiguous research tasks with little guidance, and to own a research direction end to end

- Care an unusual amount about data quality, and can dive into the data when appropriate

- Truth seeking, aiming to learn more about the science than to prove your ideas are correct

- Experience with RL algorithms for language models, scaling laws, or building RL environments and evals

- Experience with distributed training at scale and debugging problems that only show up at scale

- Experience training frontier-scale models

- Strong background in RL and machine learning fundamentals

- An excellent programmer and software engineer, comfortable working across the research stack in Python and PyTorch or JAX

- Hands-on experience training large models, through pretraining, post-training or RL

- A track record of original work in ML, such as new methods or real improvements, shown through research, open source or production impact

- MS or PhD in CS, ML, math, physics or a related field, or equivalent research experience

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

- Onsite role: must be able to work in person at the Palo Alto office

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

$220,000 - $357,000 USD

title: Care Specialist
description:
Pelago is the leading specialty substance use care provider, built on the belief that effective treatment means matching care intensity to what each member actually needs rather than defaulting to the most expensive intervention. Our programs guide members through every stage of the substance use spectrum, from unhealthy habits to active use disorders, delivering personalized treatment for tobacco, alcohol, opioid, cannabis, and stimulant use based on individual health, habits, genetics, and goals.

With Sona, our voice-first AI Mental Health Specialist, Pelago now applies that same clinically-driven model to mental health, pairing deep clinical expertise with technology to expand access without compromising care quality. We believe technology should make clinical care more precise and more human, not replace the judgment behind it.

Pelago has scaled to helping hundreds of employers and health plans and has already helped more than 750,000 members better manage their substance use. If you're passionate about AI and making an impact on the health of others, join us and make it happen!

Overview of the Role

We are seeking a Care Specialist to join our digital clinic and help members achieve healthier, more fulfilling lives. As the first point of contact, the Care Specialist plays a vital role in creating a welcoming onboarding experience and helping members successfully begin their care journey at Pelago . This role is primarily focused on conducting intake assessments, welcome calls, and initial clinical screenings, educating members on Pelago 's care model, and connecting them with the appropriate ongoing care team.

Approximately 70% of this role is dedicated to member onboarding activities, including intakes, welcome calls, and care coordination. The remaining 30% focuses on maintaining a small ongoing caseload and providing flexible clinical support through temporary member coverage, pilot initiatives, and other operational needs. The ideal candidate is clinically strong, adaptable, enjoys variety, and is passionate about improving access to high-quality substance use care.
This is a direct-service, remote clinical role based anywhere in the USA.

In this role you will…

• Serve as the first clinical point of contact for members entering Pelago , creating a welcoming, supportive onboarding experience.

• Conduct initial screenings and intake assessments to evaluate behavioral health history, substance use, symptoms, and member goals.

• Understand all Pelago care pathways, effectively communicate treatment options to members, and guide them toward the most appropriate level of care.

• Facilitate warm transitions by connecting members with their assigned counselor or coach and sharing relevant clinical information to support continuity of care.

• Conduct welcome calls and other early member touchpoints to build rapport, answer questions, increase engagement, and ensure a smooth transition into ongoing care.

• Maintain a small ongoing caseload by providing individual counseling, monitoring progress toward behavior change goals, and supporting members as needed.

• Provide temporary member coverage during clinician leave, staffing transitions, or other operational needs.

• Support special projects, pilot programs, and new clinical workflows as needed.

• Document member interactions thoroughly and contribute to ongoing quality improvement efforts.

• Utilize evidence-based approaches including CBT, Motivational Interviewing (MI), mindfulness-based interventions, harm reduction techniques, and relapse prevention.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams (including Product, Clinical, and Operations) to optimize the member experience and inform service improvements.

• Maintain active licensure(s)/certification(s) in good standing and ensure compliance with all applicable regulations.

The background we are looking for...

• 3+ years of clinical experience working with individuals with substance use disorders, with demons
